title: Position
description: data/positions/<id>.json -- one structural element (type/material/section) plus any calculated domains (docs/architecture/data-contracts.md §3.1). 1.3 (v0.94) adds `section_type` and `section`, the dimension read once by domains/section.py. 1.4 (v0.114): the record of a position Woodcore keeps itself in Woodcore-Datei/positions.json (calc/positions_store.py) -- only `position` and `type` are required; every other field may be absent or null, which reads as blank. A 1.3 record is still read. 1.5 (issue #50): a section may be a free steel profile (`kind` user, `type` USR, its `id`), and only such a record is written at 1.5.

schema_version.description: -- pinned: an export written at another version is refused rather than read as this one. 1.4 since v0.114; 1.3, whose records carried every key, is read as well; 1.5 for a record whose section is a free profile (issue #50).

material.description: What the element is made of, as typed in the Positions Element sheet (Fichte, Stahl, ...). Until the sheet gained a `resistance class` column this held the strength class; a record without `strength_class` is still read that way.

strength_class.description: The element's strength class (Festigkeitsklasse), from the Positions Element sheet's `resistance class` column: C24, GL24h, S355 ... -- what a connector's timber and a schema element's label are read off. Empty where the cell is blank.

section_type.description: The shape of the section, as typed in the Positions Element sheet's `section type` column (v0.94): rec, cir, pla, clt for timber, an SZS C5 code (IPE, HEA, ROR, RRW ...) for a steel profile, or empty. What `dimension` is read by; empty where the cell is blank or the column absent.

dimension.description: The dimension exactly as typed in the Positions Element sheet ("100/200", "200", "20/30/20/30/20", "101.6x10" ...), read according to `section_type` into `section` by domains/section.py and by nothing else (docs/domain/positions.md §7, v0.94). Facultative since v0.87: empty where the cell is blank or the column absent, and then left out of every summary with its unit. The key is always written, empty or not.

units.description: Unit the `dimension` text is given in, as typed in the Positions Element sheet (e.g. "mm"). Printed after the dimension, and only where there is one -- it qualifies the dimension and nothing else; facultative like it, and empty where the cell is blank or the column absent.

section.description: The section the row's `section_type`, `dimension` and `units` state, read once at the export (domains/section.py, v0.94) -- what the report's level-1 line prints (`text`) and what #member and a detail schema's element read, none of them parsing the dimension again. null where the type is empty and the dimension is descriptive text. Every length in mm, whatever `units` the row states.

type.description: rec, cir, pla, clt, an SZS C5 code, or USR for a free steel profile (1.5).

text.description: What a summary prints: "100/200 mm", "Ø 200 mm", "22 mm", "20/30/20/30/20 mm (120 mm)", "ROR 101.6×10" -- in the units the row states.

t.description: pla: the thickness; clt: the sum of its layers, in mm.

layers.description: clt: the layers' thicknesses, outermost first, in mm.

dims.description: steel: the designation's size as written, "101.6x10" giving [101.6, 10]; its values are SZS C5's table's (calc/norms/szs_c5.py, issue #50), read by the steel checks and not written here.

id.description: user (1.5): the id of the free profile, a file of Woodcore-Datei/profiles/ (domains/profile.py); its values are computed from its rectangles by the steel checks and not written here.

deduced.description: true where the row states no section type and its dimension reads as b/h, the case of a workbook written before the column existed: read as rec, with an export warning.

moisture_class.description: The position's moisture class (Feuchteklasse), 1, 2 or 3, from the Positions Element sheet's `moisture class` column (`Wood moisture class` until it was renamed) -- the one column of the sheet a calculation reads as a number. null where the cell is left blank, a position that is not timber having none (docs/domain/positions.md §7).

archived.description: Additive (issue #9), written only on a position deleted with its values kept («Copier les valeurs», calc/renumbering.py): the id it had and the day it was deleted. The report prints, wherever such a position is called, that the calculation stands on the values of an old position.
